tables.caption: Table 1. Concepts and symbols used in the replay
rows: Document budget K; task coverage C0 and C
K is list length; C0 is the baseline's task-document count; C is the proposed or realized count
Identify the task positions added or displaced under a finite budget
Baseline U and coverage match B(C)
U follows frozen scores; B(C) selects C task documents by those scores
Attribute the change reproduced by task allocation
Unfamiliarity and exposure
A core document contains a subclass combination absent from preceding core history; exposure counts such selected documents
Record unfamiliar documentary inputs, without measuring cognition or distinct new combinations
Unfamiliar minimum m and list N(C,m)
Require at least m unfamiliar core documents at C, preserving B(C)'s noncore identifiers
Assess selection within the same task allocation
Shortfall d and a binding requirement
d=max{0,m−n_B(C)}, where n_B(C) counts unfamiliar core documents in B(C); binding means d>0
Identify whether a feasible rule actually exchanges documents
Task-linked documents
Selected documents cited by an external task-core grant in the observation window; means are per list and totals are selection events
Compare recorded task links gained and lost, rather than inventions or adoption
General reach
Selected documents cited by at least two external organizations in the observation window
Retain broader archival reach as a separate objective
Handoff state
Source-supported direct function, mechanism analogy, unsupported match or unresolved evidence
Specify the next technical question; routes remain proposed
tables.note: Note. The main replay uses K=30 and three subsequent grant years. Repeated selection of a patent in different screens remains separate events. Strict C,m comparisons require adequate task, noncore and unfamiliar supply. The shortfall equals actual exchanges only for the specified deterministic selector; it predicts an action, not its value.

tables.caption: Table 2. Allocation and within-allocation outcomes of the novelty reservation
rows: Primary
Alternative
tables.note: Note. Means per 30-document list over the same 356 situations. Allocation contrasts compare the coverage match with baseline; within-allocation contrasts compare the novelty reservation with its coverage match. Unfamiliar exposure counts documents with an unseen core combination, not unique combinations. General reach counts documents cited by at least two external organizations. Task-linked event totals are 921/1,418/1,436 under baseline/match/novelty for the primary ranking and 1,050/1,462/1,544 for the alternative. Reproduced shares are 497/515 and 412/494. Each policy supplies 10,680 document occurrences. Repeated document selections remain separate events. The matched lists preserve the novelty lists' core counts and all noncore identifiers.

tables.caption: Table 4. Proposed routes from shortlist to technical assessment
rows: Direct function
Documented task object and thermal path; disclosed interfaces and limits; missing conditions flagged
Task engineer checks contact, insulation, leakage and operating envelope
Advance to technical feasibility review when the documented function matches the need
Mechanism analogy
Documented source function; candidate transferable principle; differences in medium, geometry and conditions
Appropriate specialist identifies adaptations and requirements for the target application
Advance as an adaptation question, with unresolved transfer conditions recorded
Unsupported match
Text showing a different object or function; no task-relevant transfer principle identified in the text examined
Analyst records the mismatch and checks any separate documented justification
Close the current task track unless further text establishes a relevant function or transfer principle
Unresolved evidence
Missing function or thermal path; exact text or claims required to decide
Analyst retrieves the specified description or claims, or defers the candidate
Keep unresolved until sufficient evidence supports another route
tables.note: Note. Routes are proposed evidence and action states illustrated by historical desk assessment. They are not measured classification accuracies, expert endorsements or tested staffing arrangements. An organization's distribution of the analyst and reviewer responsibilities may vary.
